answer: Posted collateral must equal 7 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. Because the river collateral is checked against the tide claim at intake, the zenith audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases therefore has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. That is 8 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
